news.headline: Global peace means assurance of security, dignity and justice for all: Birla
news.story_lead: Global peace means assurance of security, dignity and justice for all: Birla New Delhi, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Tuesday said the true meaning of global peace is the assurance of security, dignity and justice for all, and every citizen of the world, especially the younger generation, expects precisely this kind of future. Delivering the valedictory address at the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum here, Birla also said that while addressing the current problems, it is the responsibility of the present generations to lay the foundation of a better future for the coming generations. "The future generations will judge us by how safe, peaceful and prosperous a world we have created for them," he said.
news.full_article_text: Global peace means assurance of security, dignity and justice for all: Birla New Delhi, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Tuesday said the true meaning of global peace is the assurance of security, dignity and justice for all, and every citizen of the world, especially the younger generation, expects precisely this kind of future. Delivering the valedictory address at the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum here, Birla also said that while addressing the current problems, it is the responsibility of the present generations to lay the foundation of a better future for the coming generations. "The future generations will judge us by how safe, peaceful and prosperous a world we have created for them," he said. The speaker said the true meaning of global peace is the assurance of security, dignity, justice and a better future for all. Every citizen of the world today, especially the younger generation, expects precisely this kind of future from us," he added. Birla said the BRICS nations must work together to build a world where the sovereignty of every nation is respected, where international disputes are resolved through peaceful means and where opportunities for development are available equally to all. During the two-day conclave, the parliamentary representatives of the BRICS member nations have held meaningful deliberations on several important subjects, he said. "Our views may differ. Our opinions may also vary. Our circumstances and challenges might be different as well. However, our commitment towards the welfare of humanity, peace and prosperity remains uniform. This is the greatest strength of BRICS," he said. The speaker said that at the forum, the participants have not only discussed current challenges, but also deliberated on new possibilities for cooperation for the future. "Today, the world is facing numerous grave challenges. There is conflict and instability across various regions. There are economic uncertainties. At such a time, the importance of dialogue, trust and cooperation has increased more than ever before. "It has been India's firm belief that the permanent solution to the world's problems lies not in conflict, but in dialogue; not in war, but in peace. And more in cooperation than in competition," he said. Birla said that in a democratic system, Parliament is the most important centre for the expression of people's hopes and aspirations. "A Parliament is not merely a platform for making laws. It is also an institution of dialogue, consensus, accountability and public trust. Despite considerable diversity within our parliamentary systems, safeguarding the interests of our citizens and winning the trust of the public is our shared responsibility," he said. Therefore, it is essential that parliaments become more effective, transparent and citizen-centric with changing times, he said. Birla said that today, artificial intelligence and digital technology are transforming the ways people work and by using technology responsibly, parliamentary working methods can be made more effective and citizen participation can be strengthened. "At the same time, the efficiency and competence of our honourable members of Parliament can also be enhanced. The purpose of technology should be to improve human life. Therefore, we must also ensure that the development of technology aligns with human values. "The use of artificial intelligence must be based on the principles of ethics, transparency, accountability and human welfare. Our parliaments can make a significant contribution in this direction by sharing their experiences and best practices," the speaker said. This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text. - Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla

news.headline: Moby-Dick; Tracing the success of a Great American Novel
news.story_lead: Moby-Dick; Tracing the success of a Great American Novel It sold poorly, disappeared from print, and was largely forgotten when Herman Melville died. Moby-Dick, published 175 years ago, is now an enduring classic “Call me Ishmael” is one of the most recognisable opening lines in literature. But when Herman Melville’s Moby-Dick; or, The Whale , came out in 1851, it wasn’t immediately successful.
news.full_article_text: Moby-Dick; Tracing the success of a Great American Novel It sold poorly, disappeared from print, and was largely forgotten when Herman Melville died. Moby-Dick, published 175 years ago, is now an enduring classic “Call me Ishmael” is one of the most recognisable opening lines in literature. But when Herman Melville’s Moby-Dick; or, The Whale , came out in 1851, it wasn’t immediately successful. It sold poorly, got mixed reviews, and did nothing to revive Melville’s declining reputation. By the time he died in 1891, he and the book were largely forgotten. It took decades for that to change. How did a book that failed in its own day become one of the most studied and admired novels in American literature? The Moby-Dick that appeared in October 1851 had grown far beyond the sea adventure Melville first set out to write. He had written and rewritten it, drawing on his own experiences at sea, on the books he had read about whales and whaling, and on one of the most notorious disasters in the history of the industry. By the middle of the 19th century, whaling was big business. Whale blubber was rendered into train oil, used to lubricate machinery, and light cities. New Bedford, one of the centres of the American whaling industry, was known as “The City That Lit the World”. But the animals themselves remained largely a mystery. On November 20, 1820, a sperm whale struck the whaleship Essex in the southern Pacific. Twenty men escaped in three boats and spent about three months at sea, facing starvation and dehydration; some eventually resorted to cannibalism. One of the survivors, first mate Owen Chase, later wrote an account of the disaster. Melville read it, and the Essex became one of the sources for Moby-Dick . Chase described the whale as coming towards the ship “with twice his ordinary speed”, and said it appeared to have “tenfold fury and vengeance in his aspect”. Melville turned that single encounter into something much larger. Ishmael, an outsider who goes to sea looking for something he can’t quite name, befriends Queequeg, a tattooed harpooner, and joins the crew of the Pequod under Captain Ahab, who lost a leg to a great white sperm whale named Moby Dick. Ahab is set on finding and killing the whale. His obsession takes over the voyage, despite the objections of his first mate, Starbuck, and a whaling expedition becomes a hunt the crew can’t escape. The novel that runs into 135 chapters moves between adventure, philosophy, descriptions of whales, religious references, and long passages of whalelore. Narrative and essay-like sections are mixed together. It’s also funnier than its reputation suggests. Ishmael’s friendship with Queequeg provides some of the book’s lighter moments. “Better sleep with a sober cannibal than a drunken Christian,” he thinks, after being made to share a bed with the harpooner. Then there are the questions that keep readers coming back. Ishmael, Ahab, and the ship Rachel all have Biblical names, and the story can be read through a religious lens. Ahab’s pursuit of the whale resembles idolatry. Moby Dick can be read as a symbol of God, nature, fate or something more unknowable. Readers down the ages have found in it a story about obsession, nature, religion, race, friendship and American identity. Melville and Hawthorne Melville met Nathaniel Hawthorne on August 5, 1850, when a group of writers and publishers climbed Monument Mountain in Massachusetts. Melville was 31. Hawthorne was 46 and already well known for The Scarlet Letter. The encounter affected Melville deeply. He later wrote that Hawthorne had “dropped germinous seeds into my soul”. The two began corresponding. Soon after, Melville moved with his family to Arrowhead not far from Hawthorne. Hawthorne read Moby-Dick and praised it in a letter that has since been lost. Melville’s response survives: “Your heart beat in my ribs and mine in yours, and both in God’s...” Melville dedicated his book to Hawthorne’s “genius”. The exact nature of their friendship has been debated ever since. What’s clearer is the effect on his writing: during this period, he moved further away from the straightforward adventure story he had begun and towards the strange, symbolic, mixed-form novel that Moby-Dick ultimately became. Melville had first contracted with British publisher Richard Bentley for a book then known as The Whale . He kept the printing in New York so he could oversee the proofs while continuing to revise the manuscript, writing to Hawthorne about having to “work and slave on my ‘Whale’ while it is driving through the press”. The British edition, 500 copies, was published on October 18, 1851. The American edition followed on November 14 from Harpers, under the title Moby-Dick . The two editions differed greatly. The most important difference was that the British edition had no epilogue. That appears to have been a production error, but it mattered. Without it, British readers were left with a first-person narrator who seemed unlikely to have survived the destruction of the Pequod. The Spectator objected that “nothing should be introduced into a novel which it is physically impossible for the writer to have known”, and other reviewers asked how the author could be alive to tell the story. The American edition had the epilogue, revealing how Ishmael survives: floating on Queequeg’s coffin till he’s rescued by the Rachel. The poor British reviews didn’t help the book’s reception in America, and Melville’s career continued to decline. By 1856, Hawthorne recorded that Melville had “pretty much made up his mind to be annihilated”. When Melville died in 1891, Moby-Dick was out of print. Billy Budd , another of his major works, remained unpublished. That changed in the 20th century. Melville’s birth centenary in 1919 renewed interest in his work. Raymond Weaver’s 1921 biography, Herman Melville: Mariner and Mystic , and a 16-volume edition of Melville’s works published between 1922 and 1924 helped drive the “Melville Revival”. Every modern writer of standing from William Faulkner to DH Lawrence has been struck by Moby-Dick with the latter calling it “the greatest book of the sea ever written”. A novel that was once dismissed as too long and too strange, is now read as a sea adventure, a philosophical novel, a comedy, a tragedy, and a catalogue of what Melville knew and imagined about the natural world. Ahab’s obsession can be read as a warning about the desire to master nature; Ishmael’s curiosity points the other way. “It is not down on any map; true places never are,” he says. And it’s Ishmael who survives to tell the story. “I know not all that may be coming, but be it what it will, I’ll go to it laughing,” he says. In the decades after Melville’s death, the book that failed in his lifetime became, as The Oxford Companion to English Literature puts it, “the closest approach the United States has had to a national prose epic”. In 2026, Melville has returned to the city that helped shape the book.

news.headline: 'Govt allowing this to happen': Supreme Court questions overpricing of medicines, massive gap in MRP and cost to retailers
news.story_lead: 'Govt allowing this to happen': Supreme Court questions overpricing of medicines, massive gap in MRP and cost to retailers The SC bench questioned why the system appeared to favour pharmaceutical manufacturers and asked whether such practices should be allowed to continue unchecked The Supreme Court on Tuesday pulled up the Centre over the significant gap between the maximum retail price (MRP) of medicines and the prices at which retailers purchase them, questioning the government's oversight of drug pricing in the country. Hearing two petitions that raised concerns over medicine pricing, a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta questioned why the system appeared to favour pharmaceutical manufacturers and asked whether such practices should be allowed to continue unchecked, according to PTI. Also Read | SC orders Centre to form panel for law on unethical pharma marketing Deep Di
news.full_article_text: 'Govt allowing this to happen': Supreme Court questions overpricing of medicines, massive gap in MRP and cost to retailers The SC bench questioned why the system appeared to favour pharmaceutical manufacturers and asked whether such practices should be allowed to continue unchecked The Supreme Court on Tuesday pulled up the Centre over the significant gap between the maximum retail price (MRP) of medicines and the prices at which retailers purchase them, questioning the government's oversight of drug pricing in the country. Hearing two petitions that raised concerns over medicine pricing, a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta questioned why the system appeared to favour pharmaceutical manufacturers and asked whether such practices should be allowed to continue unchecked, according to PTI. Also Read | SC orders Centre to form panel for law on unethical pharma marketing Deep Dive “The government is allowing this to happen. It is under the government's own eyes that it is happening,” the bench told Centre. “Should it be allowed to run amok?” the bench asked. The bench also described the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), the body responsible for regulating drug prices, as appearing to be a “totally defunct” organisation. During the hearing, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, told the court that the government's policy was “that the entire ecosystem is not to be controlled”. Also Read | SC asks govt to expedite regulating prices of life saving drugs Bhati said that medicine prices in India were among the lowest in the world, arguing that the government needed to balance affordability with the availability of medicines and the broader interests of the pharmaceutical industry. The bench reserved its order in the matter. In an earlier matter heard on October 12, the top court had said the Centre's response on capping the trade margin of anti-cancer drugs at 30 per cent of the maximum retail price (MRP) was "hardly anything to be happy about" and questioned why the government cannot cap trade margins of other medicines. news.headline: Supreme Court to Formulate Guiding Principles for Compulsory Rural Service by Medical Students
news.story_lead: The Supreme Court of India has announced that it will lay down uniform guiding principles regarding compulsory rural service for medical students. The decision aims to bring clarity and standardization to rural service bond policies across various states.
news.full_article_text:
### Supreme Court Framework for Compulsory Rural Medical Service

The Supreme Court of India stated that it will formulate standardized guiding principles governing compulsory rural service for medical graduates and postgraduates across the country.

* **Standardized Guidelines:** The apex court expressed its intention to establish nationwide principles to resolve ambiguities surrounding compulsory rural service obligations.
* **Policy Streamlining:** The decision addresses variations in medical service bonds imposed by different state governments on students completing their medical education.
* **Public Interest Focus:** The initiative seeks to balance the requirement of rural healthcare availability with fair and consistent regulations for medical professionals.
bullet_points: The Supreme Court of India announced plans to formulate guiding principles for compulsory rural service for medical students.
The court aims to address policy disparities and bond requirements imposed by different state authorities.
Compulsory rural service bonds are implemented by state governments to ensure medical coverage in rural areas.
The judicial intervention seeks to provide uniform guidelines governing bond enforcement, service tenure, and conditions.

Key Initiative: Formulation of guiding principles for compulsory rural medical service
Target Group: Undergraduate and postgraduate medical students

Standardizing rural bonds balances the constitutional objective of public health access with equitable policy terms for medical professionals.

impacts: Creation of a standardized framework for compulsory rural service bonds across Indian states.
challenges: Reconciling state health policy autonomy with the need for uniform national service guidelines for medical professionals.

hindi_translation.story_lead: भारत के उच्चतम न्यायालय ने घोषणा की है कि वह मेडिकल छात्रों के लिए अनिवार्य ग्रामीण सेवा से संबंधित समान मार्गदर्शक सिद्धांत तैयार करेगा। इस निर्णय का उद्देश्य विभिन्न राज्यों में ग्रामीण सेवा बॉन्ड नीतियों में स्पष्टता और मानकीकरण लाना है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### मेडिकल छात्रों की अनिवार्य ग्रामीण सेवा पर सुप्रीम कोर्ट का ढांचा

भारत के उच्चतम न्यायालय ने कहा कि वह देश भर में मेडिकल स्नातकों और स्नातकोत्तरों के लिए अनिवार्य ग्रामीण सेवा को नियंत्रित करने वाले मानकीकृत मार्गदर्शक सिद्धांत तैयार करेगा।

* **मानकीकृत दिशानिर्देश:** शीर्ष अदालत ने अनिवार्य ग्रामीण सेवा दायित्वों से संबंधित अनिश्चितताओं को दूर करने के लिए राष्ट्रव्यापी सिद्धांत स्थापित करने की मंशा व्यक्त की।
* **नीति सुव्यवसायीकरण:** यह निर्णय विभिन्न राज्य सरकारों द्वारा चिकित्सा शिक्षा पूरी करने वाले छात्रों पर लगाए गए मेडिकल सेवा बॉन्ड में भिन्नता को संबोधित करता है।
* **जनहित पर ध्यान:** इस पहल का उद्देश्य चिकित्सा पेशेवरों के लिए निष्पक्ष और सुसंगत नियमों को बनाए रखते हुए ग्रामीण स्वास्थ्य देखभाल की उपलब्धता की आवश्यकता को संतुलित करना है।

news.headline: Pope's South American trip to go ahead as planned after lung cancer surgery
news.story_lead: - Published 26 October 2026 The Vatican has confirmed that Pope Leo will go on his South American tour as planned, following his surgery for lung cancer. He was diagnosed with lung cancer and underwent successful surgery in Rome on 13 October to remove a tumour on the lower part of his right lung. The 71-year-old is scheduled to travel to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on 6-17 November, the Vatican said, adding that the he was looking forward to it "with great joy and enthusiasm".
news.full_article_text: - Published 26 October 2026 The Vatican has confirmed that Pope Leo will go on his South American tour as planned, following his surgery for lung cancer. He was diagnosed with lung cancer and underwent successful surgery in Rome on 13 October to remove a tumour on the lower part of his right lung. The 71-year-old is scheduled to travel to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on 6-17 November, the Vatican said, adding that the he was looking forward to it "with great joy and enthusiasm". The Pope will follow the same programme as planned, visiting 10 cities on the tour. "I am looking forward to returning to the continent where I've experienced so many moments of my life," Pope Leo said. The Pope's trip will begin in Uruguay on 8 November, where he will visit the capital Montevideo, as well as other key cities. He will then travel to Argentina from November 11-17, visiting a number of places including the capital Buenos Aires. After that he will spend six days in Peru, where roughly 76% of the population are Catholic, and will include stops in Lima, Chiclayo, Cuzco and Pucallpa. Peru's Cardinal Castillo, the Archbishop of Lima, has said the trip would involve young people, women who help run community kitchens and members of the country's indigenous communities, according to Vatican News. The archbishop highlighted the Pope's close ties with the people of Chiclayo, where he lived for several years. The Pope has Peruvian citizenship. The Catholic Church sent him to Peru as a missionary in 1985 , when he was 30 years old. He joined the Augustinian mission in Chulucanas, in the Peruvian department of Piura, and the following year, joined the mission in the city of Trujillo. For almost three decades, he worked between the US and Peru. The Pope leaving Gemelli Hospital following his lung surgery on 17 October Leo announced the news of his lung operation himself to the world on 11 October during his weekly Sunday prayers, telling the crowd in St Peter's Square that doctors had found a nodule on his lung. He reassured pilgrims that the growth was "well-contained" and caught "at an early stage" but that his doctors had advised him to have it removed. The surgery lasted for 90 minutes, and he was discharged from Rome's Gemelli hospital on 17 October. The Pope's surgeon, Stefano Margaritora, said he was in an "absolutely satisfactory clinical condition", and said there were "no clinical reasons" why the trip should not go ahead. Tests showed the cancer was "localised". Since his operation, the pope has been resting and gradually resuming his work. He has been "adjusting his daily schedule in consultation with his doctors to prioritise his recovery while continuing to fulfill the responsibilities of his ministry," the Vatican said. Leo was "deeply grateful for the prayers and affection he has received from throughout the world," the Vatican said. The Vatican said Friday that Leo would cancel a planned trip to Assisi on October 27th, on the recommendation of his doctors. news.headline: MCD to procure 98,500 vials of anti-rabies vaccine
news.story_lead: MCD to procure 98,500 vials of anti-rabies vaccine The procurement of 98,500 vials, approved on Monday, is part of the MCD’s plan to acquire 1.20 lakh anti-rabies vaccine vials over the next two years The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) is set to procure 98,500 vials of anti-rabies vaccine to meet requirements over the next two years and ensure timely treatment for victims of animal bites at its hospitals and health centres. The procurement of 98,500 vials, approved on Monday, is part of the MCD’s plan to acquire 1.20 lakh anti-rabies vaccine vials over the next two years, with 21,500 vials already purchased in May 2026. “The corporation has approved a plan to procure a total of 1.20 lakh vials to meet the requirements for the next two years.
news.full_article_text: MCD to procure 98,500 vials of anti-rabies vaccine The procurement of 98,500 vials, approved on Monday, is part of the MCD’s plan to acquire 1.20 lakh anti-rabies vaccine vials over the next two years The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) is set to procure 98,500 vials of anti-rabies vaccine to meet requirements over the next two years and ensure timely treatment for victims of animal bites at its hospitals and health centres. The procurement of 98,500 vials, approved on Monday, is part of the MCD’s plan to acquire 1.20 lakh anti-rabies vaccine vials over the next two years, with 21,500 vials already purchased in May 2026. “The corporation has approved a plan to procure a total of 1.20 lakh vials to meet the requirements for the next two years. Of these, 21,500 vials were purchased in May 2026, while approval has been granted for the procurement of the remaining 98,500 vials,” said an MCD official on Monday. Also Read: Classes resume in Rajouri as authorities rein in stray dog crisis MCD Standing Committee chairperson Satya Sharma said the proposal to procure the vials for the next two years was made following an assessment of the civic body’s healthcare needs. “Providing timely treatment to victims of animal attacks is a priority for the corporation. With this objective, the MCD has assessed the requirements of its healthcare services and prepared a procurement plan to meet the vaccine requirements for the next two years,” said Sharma. MCD’s hospital administration department is undertaking the procurement at an estimated cost of ₹ 2.52 crore under a two-year rate contract for 1ml anti-rabies vaccine vials. The civic body also operates over 25 dedicated anti-rabies vaccination centres under its health department. The move is expected to benefit thousands of residents, particularly in low-income neighbourhoods, who rely on MCD-run facilities for post-exposure treatment following dog bites. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Gargi Shukla Gargi Shukla is a correspondent with Hindustan Times. news.headline: Meghalaya SIR: 2 foreigners excluded, 2.18 million electors in final roll
news.story_lead: Meghalaya SIR: 2 foreigners excluded, 2.18 million electors in final roll Both are of Nepalese origin and married to Indian women and were found to be enrolled as voters in Mawsynram On Monday, the final electoral roll in Meghalaya was published after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), with 2.18 million electors, a net increase of 14,720 from the August 5 draft roll. The two voters flagged at the draft stage as suspected foreign nationals were excluded from the final roll, and the matter was referred to the home department. HT has learnt that both men are of Nepalese origin and married to Indian women.
news.full_article_text: Meghalaya SIR: 2 foreigners excluded, 2.18 million electors in final roll Both are of Nepalese origin and married to Indian women and were found to be enrolled as voters in Mawsynram On Monday, the final electoral roll in Meghalaya was published after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), with 2.18 million electors, a net increase of 14,720 from the August 5 draft roll. The two voters flagged at the draft stage as suspected foreign nationals were excluded from the final roll, and the matter was referred to the home department. HT has learnt that both men are of Nepalese origin and married to Indian women. They were found to be enrolled as voters in the Mawsynram constituency in the East Khasi Hills district. Meghalaya chief electoral officer BDR Tiwari confirmed the two men have been excluded from the final roll and the matter has been forwarded to the appropriate agency. The two men account for roughly 0.001% of the 1,87,126 names removed during the SIR, or about one in every 93,500 deletions. The draft-stage exclusions were attributed to death (81,490), absence (45,011), shifting (42,532), duplicate entries (6,701) and other reasons (4,668). The pre-SIR roll had 2.35 million electors, and notices were issued to 6,51,735, either unmapped (2,22,786) or with logical discrepancies (4,28,949), and all hearings were completed. The logical discrepancy criteria were not part of the process in Bihar, where the SIR began in 2025. It attracted attention when the process was undertaken in West Bengal. West Bengal is the only state where electors flagged under this category face adjudication and cannot vote, making logical discrepancy notices a flashpoint. ECI’s power to verify citizenship Swapnil Tripathi of the think tank Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy said the Election Commission of India (ECI) does not have a general power to identify suspected foreign nationals, but can make a limited inquiry into a person’s claim of citizenship while revising rolls, since only citizens can be registered as voters. In the Bihar SIR judgment, the Supreme Court in May said that if the ECI is unsatisfied about a person’s citizenship, it must refer the matter to the competent authority in the central government for inquiry. Tripathi said this does not confer a blanket power on the ECI to identify or declare individuals as foreign nationals. “Its inquiry is limited to the question of eligibility for inclusion in the electoral rolls, and any deletion on grounds of citizenship remains subject to the outcome of adjudication by the competent authority.” Union Home minister Amit Shah has repeatedly emphasised the policy to “detect, delete and deport” illegal immigrants, and that the SIR aims to cleanse electoral rolls of duplicate entries and undocumented immigrants. He has accused the Opposition of protesting against the SIR to keep illegal immigrants on the rolls. Congress Jairam Ramesh questioned how many “ghuspaithiye (infiltrators)” have been detected, deleted and deported following SIR. Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge has accused the government of using the rhetoric on illegal immigration to divert attention from the alleged exclusion of millions of voters.

hindi_translation.full_article_text: Meghalaya SIR: 2 foreigners excluded, 2.18 million electors in final roll Both are of Nepalese origin and married to Indian women and were found to be enrolled as voters in Mawsynram On Monday, the final electoral roll in Meghalaya was published after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), with 2.18 million electors, a net increase of 14,720 from the August 5 draft roll. The two voters flagged at the draft stage as suspected foreign nationals were excluded from the final roll, and the matter was referred to the home department. HT has learnt that both men are of Nepalese origin and married to Indian women. They were found to be enrolled as voters in the Mawsynram constituency in the East Khasi Hills district. Meghalaya chief electoral officer BDR Tiwari confirmed the two men have been excluded from the final roll and the matter has been forwarded to the appropriate agency. The two men account for roughly 0.001% of the 1,87,126 names removed during the SIR, or about one in every 93,500 deletions. The draft-stage exclusions were attributed to death (81,490), absence (45,011), shifting (42,532), duplicate entries (6,701) and other reasons (4,668). The pre-SIR roll had 2.35 million electors, and notices were issued to 6,51,735, either unmapped (2,22,786) or with logical discrepancies (4,28,949), and all hearings were completed. The logical discrepancy criteria were not part of the process in Bihar, where the SIR began in 2025. It attracted attention when the process was undertaken in West Bengal. West Bengal is the only state where electors flagged under this category face adjudication and cannot vote, making logical discrepancy notices a flashpoint. ECI’s power to verify citizenship Swapnil Tripathi of the think tank Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy said the Election Commission of India (ECI) does not have a general power to identify suspected foreign nationals, but can make a limited inquiry into a person’s claim of citizenship while revising rolls, since only citizens can be registered as voters. In the Bihar SIR judgment, the Supreme Court in May said that if the ECI is unsatisfied about a person’s citizenship, it must refer the matter to the competent authority in the central government for inquiry. Tripathi said this does not confer a blanket power on the ECI to identify or declare individuals as foreign nationals. “Its inquiry is limited to the question of eligibility for inclusion in the electoral rolls, and any deletion on grounds of citizenship remains subject to the outcome of adjudication by the competent authority.” Union Home minister Amit Shah has repeatedly emphasised the policy to “detect, delete and deport” illegal immigrants, and that the SIR aims to cleanse electoral rolls of duplicate entries and undocumented immigrants. He has accused the Opposition of protesting against the SIR to keep illegal immigrants on the rolls. Congress Jairam Ramesh questioned how many “ghuspaithiye (infiltrators)” have been detected, deleted and deported following SIR. Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge has accused the government of using the rhetoric on illegal immigration to divert attention from the alleged exclusion of millions of voters.

news.full_article_text: Centre seeks US deportation of man who fled India despite passport lying in Supreme Court This follows steps initiated by the Supreme Court after Manish Chhokar allegedly left India in January 2025, despite his passport being in the court’s custody The Indian government has approached US authorities seeking the deportation of a man who managed to leave the country despite his passport being deposited with the Supreme Court, which is pursuing contempt proceedings against him in a child custody dispute. A bench of justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi, in an order released on Monday, recorded a communication from the Centre confirming that the Central Bureau of Investigation’s Interpol unit had written to the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) seeking the deportation of Manish Chhokar, and expressed satisfaction with the steps taken to secure his presence in India. The court adjourned the matter by four weeks, allowing the government more time to pursue the process. “In view of the steps taken by the Union of India to secure the presence of the respondent, of which we are satisfied,” it said. The case The development follows a series of steps initiated by the Supreme Court after Chhokar, a US Green Card holder, allegedly left India in January 2025 despite his Indian passport being in the court’s custody and without its permission. The court had issued a non-bailable warrant against him and subsequently directed the CBI to investigate how he managed to leave the country. The agency registered a case against him in March 2025. The latest order records that the CBI’s National Central Bureau in New Delhi sent a communication dated September 30, 2026, to the FBI at the US Embassy in New Delhi, seeking Chhokar’s deportation. The communication was enclosed with a letter dated October 13, addressed to the Legal Consultant in the ministry of external affairs, and placed before the court by the Centre’s counsel. The court had earlier explored the options available to the government to secure Chhokar’s return. In an order dated August 26, 2025, it recorded the Centre’s assessment that extradition from the US might not be feasible because contempt of court, by itself, was not an extraditable offence under the applicable framework. The government had suggested that summons could be served through US authorities under the bilateral Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty in criminal matters. It had also proposed revoking Chhokar’s Indian passport and pursuing deportation through US authorities. On July 20, 2026, the Supreme Court took note of a statement by Chhokar’s counsel that he was not in a position to travel to India. His passport was subsequently cancelled, and the October 15 order was recorded, leaving the government to pursue the course outlined in its earlier note. The contempt proceedings The contempt proceedings arise from a settlement reached before the Supreme Court in October 2019 between Chhokar and his former wife, following their marital dispute. The settlement included an undertaking by him to hand over custody of their son to his former wife. When he allegedly failed to comply with the arrangement, contempt proceedings were initiated. The court had directed him to remain personally present during the proceedings, but was informed in January 2025 that he had left for the US. Taking serious exception to his departure, the court had then issued a non-bailable warrant and directed the Union government to take every possible step under the law to secure his arrest and return. It also asked the Centre to ascertain how he had been permitted to leave the country without his passport and who had assisted him. The CBI subsequently registered an FIR following a preliminary inquiry. According to the agency’s allegations, Chhokar departed from Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport for the US on January 20, 2025, using a re-entry permit issued by the American Embassy, despite not having his Indian passport with him. The FIR contended that he obtained emigration clearance by providing false information about the whereabouts of his passport and his proposed travel documentation. These allegations are subject to investigation. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Utkarsh Anand Utkarsh Anand is the National Legal Editor at Hindustan Times, where he leads the newspaper's coverage of the Supreme Court, constitutional law, the judiciary and the Union law ministry. He joined Hindustan Times in 2020 after stints at Press Trust of India (PTI), The Indian Express and CNN-News18, and has over two decades of experience reporting on law, governance and public policy. His work has focussed on some of India's most consequential constitutional and legal developments, including the Supreme Court's judgments on Article 370, marriage equality, decriminalisation of homosexuality, the Babri Masjid dispute, electoral reforms and judicial appointments. He specialises in making complex legal proceedings and judgments accessible to readers while examining their wider social and political impact. Beyond daily reportage, Utkarsh has led investigative projects and enterprise reporting that have shaped public debate and prompted institutional responses. His work has received several journalism awards, including the Ramnath Goenka Excellence in Journalism Award. As National Legal Editor, he has also played a key role in expanding Hindustan Times' legal journalism footprint, mentoring reporters and strengthening coverage across platforms. A Chevening South Asia Journalism Programme Fellow, Utkarsh regularly writes analyses on the judiciary and constitutional issues, and his reporting is widely followed by lawyers, judges, policymakers, academics and readers seeking clarity on India's evolving legal landscape. According to the agency’s allegations, Chhokar departed from Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport for the US on January 20, 2025, using a re-entry permit issued by the American Embassy, despite not having his Indian passport with him. The FIR contended that he obtained emigration clearance by providing false information about the whereabouts of his passport and his proposed travel documentation. bullet_points: Centre seeks US deportation of man who fled India despite passport lying in Supreme Court
This follows steps initiated by the Supreme Court after Manish Chhokar allegedly left India in January 2025, despite his passport being in the court’s custody

The Indian government has approached US authorities seeking the deportation of a man who managed to leave the country despite his passport being deposited with the Supreme Court, which is pursuing contempt proceedings against him in a child custody dispute.

A bench of justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi, in an order released on Monday, recorded a communication from the Centre confirming that the Central Bureau of Investigation’s Interpol unit had written to the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) seeking the deportation of Manish Chhokar, and expressed satisfaction with the steps taken to secure his presence in India.
The court adjourned the matter by four weeks, allowing the government more time to pursue the process.
“In view of the steps taken by the Union of India to secure the presence of the respondent, of which we are satisfied,” it said.

The development follows a series of steps initiated by the Supreme Court after Chhokar, a US Green Card holder, allegedly left India in January 2025 despite his Indian passport being in the court’s custody and without its permission. The court had issued a non-bailable warrant against him and subsequently directed the CBI to investigate how he managed to leave the country.
The agency registered a case against him in March 2025.

hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### साई कोलकाता ने एशियाई खेलों के पदक विजेताओं का किया सम्मान

भारतीय खेल प्राधिकरण (SAI) के कोलकाता स्थित पूर्वी क्षेत्रीय केंद्र ने एशियाई खेलों में स्वर्ण और कांस्य पदक जीतने वाले एथलीटों को सम्मानित करने के लिए एक विशेष समारोह आयोजित किया।

### प्रमुख बिंदु
- **समारोह का उद्देश्य**: एशियाई खेलों में पदक जीतने वाले एथलीटों का सम्मान करना और नए खिलाड़ियों को प्रेरित करना।
- **आयोजक संस्था**: भारतीय खेल प्राधिकरण (साई) नेताजी सुभाष पूर्वी केंद्र, कोलकाता।
- **महत्व**: अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मंच पर भारत का मान बढ़ाने वाले खिलाड़ियों की उपलब्धियों को रेखांकित करना तथा क्षेत्रीय खेल बुनियादी ढांचे की भूमिका को उजागर करना।

### क्षेत्रीय साई केंद्रों की भूमिका
साई के क्षेत्रीय केंद्र भारत भर में उत्कृष्ट एथलीट प्रशिक्षण, प्रतिभा पहचान और खेल विज्ञान सहायता के मुख्य केंद्र के रूप में कार्य करते हैं।

news.headline: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla Opens 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum in New Delhi
news.story_lead: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla inaugurated the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum at Samvidhan Sadan in New Delhi, calling on member states to translate inter-parliamentary dialogue into concrete legislative results. The two-day conference centers on people-centric development, sustainability, and resilience against the backdrop of rising global economic and geopolitical instability.
news.full_article_text:
### 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum Convened in New Delhi

Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla inaugurated the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum at Samvidhan Sadan within the Parliament House Complex in New Delhi. Addressing legislative delegations from BRICS member and partner nations, Birla highlighted that the real success of international groupings lies in translating high-level policy declarations into measurable improvements in citizens' daily lives. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also engaged with visiting parliamentary delegations during the event.

### Core Theme and Focus Areas

The two-day forum is structured around the central theme, “Strengthening Parliaments for People-Centric Development.” Discussions aim to address pressing global issues including financial volatility, trade frictions, regional military conflicts, terrorism, and climate change. Speaker Birla noted that legislatures hold a unique responsibility to foster mutual trust, bridge political divides, and facilitate peaceful resolution of global crises through lawmaking, budgetary approvals, and institutional oversight.

### Global South and Institutional Development

A key focus of the address was amplifying the voice of the Global South in international policy decision-making. Birla urged parliamentarians to ensure that the priorities of developing countries lead to responsive national policies rather than remaining limited to non-binding joint declarations. Additionally, he highlighted the importance of empowering the youth, urging legislative bodies to channel technological capability and youth creativity into broad-based nation-building efforts.

### Bilateral Engagements and Pre-Forum Talks

Reflecting Prime Minister Modi’s vision of developing BRICS into an “ecosystem of solutions,” Birla emphasized evaluating the forum based on actionable legislative outcomes. Ahead of the formal opening, Speaker Birla conducted a bilateral meeting with a Russian parliamentary delegation led by Vyacheslav Volodin, Chairman of the State Duma. Their discussions focused on counter-terrorism cooperation, coordination at international legislative forums, and strengthening bilateral parliamentary relations.
news.background_context: The forum builds upon India's prior chairship of the BRICS Summit of Heads of State in New Delhi, where member nations unanimously adopted a joint declaration emphasizing multilateral reform and collective economic cooperation.

hindi_translation.headline: लोकसभा अध्यक्ष ओम बिरला ने नई दिल्ली में 12वें ब्रिक्स संसदीय मंच का उद्घाटन किया
hindi_translation.story_lead: लोकसभा अध्यक्ष ओम बिरला ने नई दिल्ली स्थित संविधान सदन में 12वें ब्रिक्स संसदीय मंच का उद्घाटन किया और सदस्य देशों से संसदीय संवाद को ठोस विधायी परिणामों में बदलने का आह्वान किया। यह दो दिवसीय सम्मेलन वैश्विक आर्थिक और भू-राजनीतिक अनिश्चितता के बीच जन-केंद्रित विकास, स्थिरता और लचीलेपन पर केंद्रित है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### नई दिल्ली में आयोजित हुआ 12वां ब्रिक्स संसदीय मंच

लोकसभा अध्यक्ष ओम बिरला ने नई दिल्ली में संसद भवन परिसर स्थित संविधान सदन में 12वें ब्रिक्स संसदीय मंच का उद्घाटन किया। ब्रिक्स सदस्य और भागीदार देशों के संसदीय प्रतिनिधिमंडलों को संबोधित करते हुए, बिरला ने रेखांकित किया कि अंतर्राष्ट्रीय समूहों की वास्तविक सफलता उच्च-स्तरीय नीतिगत घोषणाओं को नागरिकों के दैनिक जीवन में मापने योग्य सुधारों में बदलने में निहित है। कार्यक्रम के दौरान प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने भी आने वाले संसदीय प्रतिनिधिमंडलों से मुलाकात की।

### मुख्य विषय और ध्यान केंद्रित क्षेत्र

दो दिवसीय मंच का मुख्य विषय "जन-केंद्रित विकास के लिए संसदों को मजबूत करना" है। इस चर्चा का उद्देश्य वित्तीय अस्थिरता, व्यापार तनाव, क्षेत्रीय सैन्य संघर्ष, आतंकवाद और जलवायु परिवर्तन सहित महत्वपूर्ण वैश्विक मुद्दों को संबोधित करना है। अध्यक्ष बिरला ने उल्लेख किया कि कानून निर्माण, बजटीय स्वीकृति और संस्थागत निगरानी के माध्यम से आपसी विश्वास को बढ़ावा देने, राजनीतिक मतभेदों को पाटने और वैश्विक संकटों के शांतिपूर्ण समाधान की सुविधा प्रदान करने की विशिष्ट जिम्मेदारी संसदों की है।

### ग्लोबल साउथ और संस्थागत विकास

संबोधन का एक प्रमुख बिंदु वैश्विक नीति निर्माण में ग्लोबल साउथ की आवाज को मजबूत करना था। बिरला ने सांसदों से यह सुनिश्चित करने का आग्रह किया कि विकासशील देशों की प्राथमिकताएं गैर-बाध्यकारी संयुक्त घोषणाओं तक सीमित रहने के बजाय उत्तरदायी राष्ट्रीय नीतियों में परिवर्तित हों। इसके अतिरिक्त, उन्होंने युवाओं के सशक्तीकरण पर जोर दिया और विधायी निकायों से तकनीकी क्षमताओं और युवाओं की रचनात्मकता को राष्ट्र-निर्माण के प्रयासों में लगाने का आह्वान किया।

### द्विपक्षीय वार्ताएं और मंच से पूर्व बैठकें

ब्रिक्स को "समाधानों का एक पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र" बनाने के प्रधानमंत्री मोदी के दृष्टिकोण को दोहराते हुए, बिरला ने केवल व्यापक चर्चाओं के बजाय ठोस परिणामों के आधार पर मंच का मूल्यांकन करने पर बल दिया। औपचारिक उद्घाटन से पहले, अध्यक्ष बिरला ने स्टेट ड्यूमा के अध्यक्ष व्याचेस्लाव वोलोडिन के नेतृत्व वाले रूसी संसदीय प्रतिनिधिमंडल के साथ द्विपक्षीय बैठक की। उनकी चर्चा आतंकवाद विरोधी सहयोग, अंतर्राष्ट्रीय संसदीय मंचों पर समन्वय और द्विपक्षीय संसदीय संबंधों को गहरा करने पर केंद्रित थी।
hindi_translation.background_context: यह मंच नई दिल्ली में आयोजित ब्रिक्स राष्ट्राध्यक्षों के शिखर सम्मेलन में भारत की पिछली अध्यक्षता पर आधारित है, जहां सदस्य देशों ने बहुपक्षीय सुधार और साझा आर्थिक सहयोग पर जोर देने वाले एक संयुक्त वक्तव्य को सर्वसम्मति से अपनाया था।
bullet_points: लोकसभा अध्यक्ष ओम बिरला ने नई दिल्ली के संविधान सदन में दो दिवसीय 12वें ब्रिक्स संसदीय मंच का उद्घाटन किया।
मंच का विषय 'जन-केंद्रित विकास के लिए संसदों को मजबूत करना' है।
कार्यक्रम के दौरान प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने आए हुए संसदीय प्रतिनिधिमंडलों से बातचीत की।
बिरला ने सदस्य देशों से प्रभावी कानून निर्माण और निगरानी के माध्यम से नीतिगत घोषणाओं को ठोस परिणामों में बदलने का आग्रह किया।
मंच ने वैश्विक शासन और निर्णय लेने की संरचनाओं में ग्लोबल साउथ की स्थिति को मजबूत करने पर बल दिया।
राष्ट्र-निर्माण के लिए युवाओं को सशक्त बनाने और तकनीकी क्षमताओं के उपयोग को प्राथमिकता दी गई।
कार्यक्रम से पहले, बिरला ने रूसी स्टेट ड्यूमा के अध्यक्ष व्याचेस्लाव वोलोडिन के साथ आतंकवाद विरोध और अंतर्राष्ट्रीय समन्वय पर द्विपक्षीय चर्चा की।
मंच ने मजबूत संस्थाओं के निर्माण के लिए आर्थिक प्रगति और पर्यावरण संरक्षण में संतुलन बनाने पर जोर दिया।

news.headline: Election Commission Informs Supreme Court of Unanimous Decisions on Electoral Roll Revision Orders
news.story_lead: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has submitted to the Supreme Court that its directives concerning electoral roll revision orders were adopted unanimously. The official submission clarifies the institutional decision-making process before the apex court in ongoing proceedings related to voter list maintenance.
news.full_article_text:
### Election Commission Submission to Supreme Court

The Election Commission of India (ECI) informed the Supreme Court that all orders and directives regarding the revision of electoral rolls were taken unanimously by the commission.

* **Unanimous Decision-Making:** The Commission emphasized that the administrative guidelines and procedural directives issued for revising voter lists reflected complete internal consensus.
* **Apex Court Proceedings:** This clarification was presented as part of legal filings before the Supreme Court concerning electoral management protocols and voter registration revisions.
* **Constitutional Duty:** The ECI highlighted its continuous obligation to ensure accurate, updated, and transparent electoral rolls across all constituencies.

hindi_translation.headline: चुनाव आयोग ने सर्वोच्च न्यायालय को सूचित किया: मतदाता सूची संशोधन आदेशों पर 'सर्वसम्मति' से लिया गया निर्णय
hindi_translation.story_lead: भारत निर्वाचन आयोग (ECI) ने सर्वोच्च न्यायालय में एक हलफनामा देकर स्पष्ट किया है कि मतदाता सूची संशोधन से जुड़े उसके आदेश सर्वसम्मति से पारित किए गए थे। यह बयान शीर्ष अदालत के समक्ष चुनाव प्रशासन से संबंधित सुनवाई के दौरान दिया गया।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### सर्वोच्च न्यायालय में चुनाव आयोग की दलील

भारत निर्वाचन आयोग (ECI) ने सर्वोच्च न्यायालय को अवगत कराया कि मतदाता सूची के पुनरीक्षण और संशोधन से जुड़े सभी आदेश आयोग द्वारा सर्वसम्मति से लिए गए थे।

* **सर्वसम्मति से निर्णय:** आयोग ने रेखांकित किया कि मतदाता सूची को अद्यतन करने के संबंध में जारी प्रशासनिक दिशा-निर्देशों में आंतरिक स्तर पर पूर्ण सहमति थी।
* **शीर्ष अदालत में कार्यवाही:** यह स्पष्टीकरण चुनावी प्रबंधन और मतदाता सूची प्रक्रियाओं से जुड़े मामले की सुनवाई के दौरान प्रस्तुत किया गया।
* **संवैधानिक दायित्व:** निर्वाचन आयोग ने लोकतांत्रिक प्रक्रियाओं की पारदर्शिता बनाए रखने के लिए मतदाता सूचियों के नियमित संशोधन के प्रति अपनी प्रतिबद्धता दोहराई।
bullet_points: भारत निर्वाचन आयोग ने सर्वोच्च न्यायालय में आधिकारिक बयान दर्ज कराया।
आयोग ने कहा कि मतदाता सूची संशोधन से संबंधित आदेश सर्वसम्मति से लिए गए थे।
यह वक्तव्य मतदाता सूची संबंधी निर्देशों पर आयोग के भीतर पूर्ण सहमति को दर्शाता है।
यह मामला चुनाव प्रशासन से जुड़ी अदालती कार्यवाही के दौरान सामने आया।
key_facts: निर्वाचन आयोग ने सर्वोच्च न्यायालय से कहा कि मतदाता सूची संशोधन के आदेश सर्वसम्मत थे।
यह प्रस्तुति सुप्रीम कोर्ट के समक्ष दायर हलफनामे/याचिका में की गई।
important_dates: 2026-10-27: सर्वोच्च न्यायालय में निर्वाचन आयोग के वक्तव्य की रिपोर्ट की तिथि।

news.headline: Celebrations in Serbia after veteran ruler Vučić loses election to student-led protest movement
news.story_lead: Watch: Joy and disbelief on Serbian streets as VuÄiÄ concedes election defeat - Published 25 October 2026 Serbia's long-standing leader Aleksandar VuÄiÄ has admitted defeat to a student-led protest movement in snap parliamentary elections. Celebrations erupted as crowds descended on the centre of Belgrade, Novi Sad and other cities. The student movement was formed less than two years ago in response to a railway station disaster blamed on corruption and negligence, but fought the election with candidates from a cross-section of Serbian society.
news.full_article_text: Watch: Joy and disbelief on Serbian streets as VuÄiÄ concedes election defeat - Published 25 October 2026 Serbia's long-standing leader Aleksandar VuÄiÄ has admitted defeat to a student-led protest movement in snap parliamentary elections. Celebrations erupted as crowds descended on the centre of Belgrade, Novi Sad and other cities. The student movement was formed less than two years ago in response to a railway station disaster blamed on corruption and negligence, but fought the election with candidates from a cross-section of Serbian society. "It is clear we have lost these elections," right-wing populist leader VuÄiÄ said as he conceded. With 97% of polling stations counted, Serbia's election commission said the students had won 2.25 million votes and the former ruling party 1.67 million. The students had secured 52.7% of the vote, while VuÄiÄ's Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) was on 39.2%, according to its preliminary figures late on Monday morning. VuÄiÄ had spent two terms as president and could not seek a third term, so was leading his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) with the aim of returning to the post of prime minister, which he left in 2017. He called the snap elections after two years of protests triggered by the collapse of a canopy in front of Novi Sad station which killed 16 people. VuÄiÄ said early results made it "clear" that his party had lost The Student List's lead candidate Ilija SrdanoviÄ told BBC Serbian: "This will be a free state." He said the anti-corruption movement, which had attracted anti-government voters across Serbia, hoped to "free the country from tyranny". There were celebrations on the streets of the city, with people dancing and chanting "victory", cars honking, and fireworks set off. "Serbia is free," one student told the BBC. "It's a miracle." - How a movement of students brought down Serbia's VuÄiÄ Published 8 hours ago During a celebration speech, Student List candidate Radomir Saicic said Serbians had shown "no obstacle was greater than their will", Reuters reported. "No force can forever overpower a people who have decided to take their destiny into their own hands," he added. Amid scenes of people dancing in the streets Belgrade, Selena Lebovic said the result was "really fabulous". "We are all crying, and what to say. We couldn't believe that it would be so easy," she told Reuters. An aerial photo shows the size of the celebrations by Students' List supporters at Slavija square in Belgrade VuÄiÄ made his announcement at the headquarters of his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in the capital Belgrade. The centre of Novi Sad - the northern city that triggered the student-led protests - was crowded. "Everything is going to get better now," David VasiÄ, one of those celebrating, told BBC Serbian. The Student List - which has no obvious leaders and whose members are not used to politics - had attracted anti-government voters across Serbia. It decided to field candidates to the 250-member parliament from across Serbian society including doctors, actors, academics and sports personalities. "This is not an ordinary election victory, this is an avalanche that has wiped out an authoritarian regime and entire political scene," said NebojÅ¡a VladisavljeviÄ, professor of political science at the University of Belgrade. There were now two big political groups in Serbia, and the Student List had "absolute legitimacy" to govern for the coming years, he told BBC Serbian. The anti-corruption movement campaigned on a manifesto that included purging officials who broke rules cracking down on protesters, stopping party loyalists from leading public enterprises, and freeing the public broadcaster of political control. VuÄiÄ and the SNS party have repeatedly denied corruption. VuÄiÄ, who backed Serbia's candidacy for the European Union while refusing to impose sanctions on Russia over its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, had pledged to increase pensions and public sector salaries, and investment in state healthcare. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov praised VuÄiÄ's contribution to relations with Russia and hoped "the new political force" in Belgrade would understand that co-operation with Moscow was in Serbia's interests: "But, as you know, it takes two to tango." His defeat was welcomed by Hungary's prime minister, PÃ©ter Magyar, who said he was delighted to hear from the Student List's leaders "how much strength our victory in April had given them". Magyar's party ended 16 years of Viktor OrbÃ¡n rule, while VuÄiÄ's SNS party had been in power since 2012. Ilija SrdanoviÄ, Student List's leading candidate, pictured during celebrations late on Sunday European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos said "a new chapter can begin for Serbia. The door to the EU is open, and we are ready to move forward together". Earlier in the day, long queues were seen outside polling stations in cities and towns across Serbia. This was also the case outside booths in a number of countries with sizeable Serbian communities - including Slovenia's capital Ljubljana, Germany's Munich, and Los Angeles and Chicago in the US. In France, Serbian voters waited in line in heavy rain in Paris. The election was held amid high tensions across Serbia, with police sealing off streets around the Republic Electoral Commission (RIK) in Belgrade. Attention will now turn to who will lead the Student List as prime minister. Presidential elections are due to take place in December, with parliament speaker Ana BrnabiÄ currently filling the role in a caretaker capacity. Related topics

news.headline: Supreme Court Directs No Action Against Deleted Voters Re-Applying Via Form 6
news.story_lead: The Supreme Court of India stated that no adverse action should be taken against voters whose names have been deleted from electoral lists if they submit Form 6 for re-inclusion. news.full_article_text:
### Supreme Court Order on Voter Deletions and Form 6

The Supreme Court of India has provided relief to voters whose names were removed from electoral rolls, holding that no action should be initiated against such voters when they apply for re-inclusion using Form 6. Form 6 is the standard statutory application used by individuals seeking enrolment in electoral lists.

### Provision of Time for Document Submission

Addressing concerns over legitimate electors being left out during voter list revisions, the Supreme Court stated that genuine voters will be granted sufficient time to submit their papers if their names are omitted from the final electoral list. The directive ensures procedural fairness and protects eligible citizens from sudden disenfranchisement while navigating the process of voter roll restoration.
bullet_points: The Supreme Court declared that voters whose names were deleted will face no adverse action if they use Form 6 to re-apply.
Form 6 is the official application mechanism for inclusion of names in the electoral roll.
The Supreme Court affirmed that genuine citizens left out of the final voter list will be granted adequate time to submit supporting documents.
The order safeguards voter rights against administrative or procedural exclusions during electoral roll updates.
The decision emphasizes protecting eligible electors from disenfranchisement.

hindi_translation.headline: फॉर्म 6 का उपयोग करने वाले हटाए गए मतदाताओं पर कोई कार्रवाई नहीं होगी: उच्चतम न्यायालय
hindi_translation.story_lead: भारत के उच्चतम न्यायालय ने निर्देश दिया है कि मतदाता सूची से नाम हटाए जाने के बाद फॉर्म 6 का उपयोग करके पुन: आवेदन करने वाले मतदाताओं पर कोई प्रतिकूल कार्रवाई न की जाए। शीर्ष अदालत ने आश्वासन दिया कि अंतिम मतदाता सूची से बाहर रहे वास्तविक मतदाताओं को दस्तावेज प्रस्तुत करने के लिए पर्याप्त समय दिया जाएगा।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### फॉर्म 6 और हटाए गए मतदाताओं पर उच्चतम न्यायालय का निर्देश

भारत के उच्चतम न्यायालय ने उन मतदाताओं को राहत दी है जिनके नाम मतदाता सूची से हटा दिए गए थे। न्यायालय ने कहा कि यदि ऐसे मतदाता फॉर्म 6 के माध्यम से पुनः नामांकन के लिए आवेदन करते हैं तो उनके खिलाफ कोई कार्रवाई नहीं की जानी चाहिए। फॉर्म 6 मतदाता सूची में नाम शामिल करने के लिए उपयोग किया जाने वाला आधिकारिक वैधानिक आवेदन पत्र है।

### दस्तावेज जमा करने के लिए समय सीमा

मतदाता सूची संशोधनों के दौरान वास्तविक मतदाताओं के बाहर छूट जाने की चिंताओं को संबोधित करते हुए, उच्चतम न्यायालय ने स्पष्ट किया कि यदि अंतिम मतदाता सूची में नाम शामिल नहीं है, तो वास्तविक नागरिकों को आवश्यक दस्तावेज प्रस्तुत करने के लिए उचित समय दिया जाएगा। यह कदम मतदान के अधिकारों की रक्षा करता है और पात्र मतदाताओं को प्रक्रियात्मक त्रुटियों के कारण मताधिकार से वंचित होने से बचाता है।

news.headline: Supreme Court Collegium Recommends New Chief Justices for Four High Courts
news.story_lead: The Supreme Court Collegium, headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, has recommended the appointment of new Chief Justices for the High Courts of Delhi, Gujarat, Telangana, and Uttarakhand. These recommendations follow the elevation of former High Court Chief Justices to the Supreme Court.
news.full_article_text:
### Judicial Appointments: Collegium Recommendations

The Supreme Court Collegium passed a formal resolution recommending four judges for appointment as Chief Justices across four major High Courts in India.

### Collegium Composition
- **Head:** Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant
- **Members:** Justice Vikram Nath and Justice BV Nagarathna

### Key Recommendations for Chief Justices
- **Delhi High Court:** Justice P Sam Koshy (Currently Acting Chief Justice of Telangana High Court; parent High Court: Chhattisgarh).
- **Gujarat High Court:** Justice Manash Ranjan Pathak (Currently Judge at Gujarat High Court; parent High Court: Gauhati).
- **Telangana High Court:** Justice Tapabrata Chakraborty (Currently Judge at Calcutta High Court).
- **Uttarakhand High Court:** Justice Sudhir Singh (Currently Judge at Patna High Court).

### Context of Vacancies
The vacancies in the High Courts of Gujarat, Delhi, and Telangana arose following the elevation of their respective Chief Justices to the Supreme Court of India:
- **Justice Sunita Agarwal** (former CJ, Gujarat High Court) elevated to Supreme Court.
- **Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya** (former CJ, Delhi High Court) elevated to Supreme Court.
- **Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh** (former CJ, Telangana High Court) elevated to Supreme Court.
news.background_context: The judicial vacancies at the chief justice level in the High Courts of Gujarat, Delhi, and Telangana were created after Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, and Aparesh Kumar Singh were elevated to the Supreme Court of India and took oath as apex court judges.
bullet_points: Supreme Court Collegium recommended judges for Chief Justice positions in Delhi, Gujarat, Telangana, and Uttarakhand High Courts.
The Collegium panel was headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, along with Justices Vikram Nath and BV Nagarathna.
Justice P Sam Koshy recommended as Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court.
Justice Manash Ranjan Pathak recommended as Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court.
Justice Tapabrata Chakraborty recommended as Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court.
Justice Sudhir Singh recommended as Chief Justice of the Uttarakhand High Court.
Justice Koshy's parent High Court is Chhattisgarh, and he was serving as Acting Chief Justice of Telangana High Court.
Justice Pathak's parent High Court is Gauhati, currently serving in Gujarat High Court.
Vacancies arose following Supreme Court elevations of former High Court Chief Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, and Aparesh Kumar Singh.
key_facts: CJI Surya Kant headed the three-member SC Collegium panel.

exam_relevance: Prelims: Constitutional provisions regarding the appointment of High Court Chief Justices (Article 217), composition of the SC Collegium, and judicial transfers/elevations.
Mains (GS Paper II): Indian Judiciary, Collegium system, judicial appointments process, and structural efficiency of Higher Judiciary.
news.upsc_analysis: The judicial appointment process in India relies heavily on the Collegium system for recommending judges and Chief Justices across High Courts and the Supreme Court. The latest resolution maintains institutional leadership across four key state High Courts following consequential elevations to the Supreme Court. Understanding the distinction between a judge's parent High Court and their current court of service is crucial for constitutional studies regarding judicial administration.

hindi_translation.story_lead: भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश सूर्य कांत की अध्यक्षता वाले सुप्रीम कोर्ट कॉलेजियम ने दिल्ली, गुजरात, तेलंगाना और उत्तराखंड उच्च न्यायालयों में नए मुख्य न्यायाधीशों की नियुक्ति की सिफारिश की है। ये सिफारिशें पूर्व मुख्य न्यायाधीशों की उच्चतम न्यायालय में पदोन्नति के बाद की गई हैं।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### न्यायिक नियुक्तियां: कॉलेजियम की सिफारिशें

सुप्रीम कोर्ट कॉलेजियम ने एक प्रस्ताव पारित कर देश के चार प्रमुख उच्च न्यायालयों में मुख्य न्यायाधीशों के रूप में नियुक्ति के लिए चार न्यायाधीशों के नामों की सिफारिश की है।

### कॉलेजियम की संरचना
- **अध्यक्ष:** भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश (CJI) सूर्य कांत
- **सदस्य:** न्यायमूर्ति विक्रम नाथ और न्यायमूर्ति बी.वी. नागरत्ना

### मुख्य न्यायाधीशों के लिए प्रमुख सिफारिशें
- **दिल्ली उच्च न्यायालय:** न्यायमूर्ति पी सैम कोशी (वर्तमान में तेलंगाना उच्च न्यायालय के कार्यवाहक मुख्य न्यायाधीश; मूल उच्च न्यायालय: छत्तीसगढ़)।
- **गुजरात उच्च न्यायालय:** न्यायमूर्ति मानस रंजन पाठक (वर्तमान में गुजरात उच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश; मूल उच्च न्यायालय: गुवाहाटी)।
- **तेलंगाना उच्च न्यायालय:** न्यायमूर्ति तापब्रत चक्रवर्ती (वर्तमान में कलकत्ता उच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश)।
- **उत्तराखंड उच्च न्यायालय:** न्यायमूर्ति सुधीर सिंह (वर्तमान में पटना उच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश)।

### रिक्तियों का संदर्भ
गुजरात, दिल्ली और तेलंगाना उच्च न्यायालयों में मुख्य न्यायाधीशों के पद हाल ही में इनके मुख्य न्यायाधीशों की सर्वोच्च न्यायालय में पदोन्नति के बाद रिक्त हुए थे:
- **न्यायमूर्ति सुनीता अग्रवाल** (पूर्व मुख्य न्यायाधीश, गुजरात उच्च न्यायालय) सर्वोच्च न्यायालय में पदोन्नत।
- **न्यायमूर्ति देवेंद्र कुमार उपाध्याय** (पूर्व मुख्य न्यायाधीश, दिल्ली उच्च न्यायालय) सर्वोच्च न्यायालय में पदोन्नत।
- **न्यायमूर्ति अपरेश कुमार सिंह** (पूर्व मुख्य न्यायाधीश, तेलंगाना उच्च न्यायालय) सर्वोच्च न्यायालय में पदोन्नत।

news.exam_corner_topic: ECI Affidavit on Special Intensive Revision & Voter Registration Rules
static_gk: The Election Commission of India (ECI) is a constitutional body established under Article 324 of the Constitution of India.
Section 28 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 empowers the Central Government, in consultation with the ECI, to make rules such as the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.

Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 mandates that decisions of the ECI should ideally be unanimous, and in case of disagreement, decided by majority.
Form 6 under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 is the statutory application form for inclusion of a person's name in an electoral roll.
news.headline: ECI Tells Supreme Court All SIR Decisions Were Unanimous, Denies Statutory Amendment to Form 6
news.story_lead: The Election Commission of India (ECI) submitted a joint counter-affidavit to the Supreme Court stating that all three Special Intensive Revision (SIR) orders were passed unanimously by its three-member panel. The poll body refuted allegations that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar acted unilaterally or that statutory voter registration forms were illegally altered.
news.full_article_text:
### ECI Affidavit in Supreme Court: Key Submissions and Regulatory Arguments

In a joint counter-affidavit filed through Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu, the Election Commission of India (ECI)—represented by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi—refuted claims of unilateral decision-making during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The response came in answer to petitions, including one filed by Opposition leaders led by Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi, seeking judicial intervention and an independent probe into ECI's administrative functioning.

### Key Factual Highlights and Statutory Directives:
- **Unanimity in Decisions:** ECI affirmed that all three SIR orders—dated June 24, 2025, October 27, 2025, and May 14, 2026—were issued in full compliance with Article 324 of the Constitution and Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.
- **Status of Form 6:** The ECI clarified that Form 6, the statutory form under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 used for enrolling new voters, was never amended. The additional declaration required during SIR (initially designated as Annexure D and later substituted as Annexure IV) was a separate administrative document prescribed via SIR orders and not a modification of the statutory form.
- **Objective of Additional Declaration:** The separate declaration allowed applicants to establish linkage with previous electoral rolls (or through parents/grandparents) to eliminate the requirement of submitting supporting documents during the claims and objections phase.
- **Statutory Amendment Framework:** Under Section 28 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, any amendment to statutory rules or forms must be notified by the Central Government in consultation with ECI and presented before Parliament. ECI maintained this procedure was not required since Form 6 itself remained unchanged.
- **Internal Deliberations vs Final Decisions:** Clarifying reports of internal friction, ECI noted that routine queries or internal notes raised by commissioners do not constitute formal decisions under Section 18 of the 2023 Act. Deliberations culminate in formal decisions recorded on files or during meetings.
- **Clarification on Communication with Cabinet Secretary:** ECI stated that July 29, 2026 correspondence sent by Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi to the Cabinet Secretary concerned administrative deputation and internal work distribution of an IAS officer, not policy or IT management. An office order dated July 28, 2026 was stayed following a joint direction on July 30, 2026 and never executed.
news.background_context: The matter stems from petitions challenging the legality of nationwide SIR operations and allegations based on media reports that two election commissioners had dissented on 14 occasions regarding voter management and IT infrastructure. Opposition leaders sought suspension of SIR, production of internal file notings, and a retired Supreme Court judge-led inquiry into ECINET and ERONET databases.

Affidavit states all three SIR orders (June 24, 2025; October 27, 2025; May 14, 2026) were decided unanimously.
ECI denied modifying Form 6 under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.

Opposition petition led by Rahul Gandhi sought a judge-led inquiry and halt to ongoing SIR exercises.
ECI clarified that internal correspondence on July 29, 2026 related to staff deputation, not election policy decisions.

news.upsc_analysis: The counter-affidavit filed by the Election Commission highlights the operational boundary between statutory modifications requiring parliamentary oversight and administrative addendums issued under constitutional authority. It underscores how Section 18 of the 2023 Act enforces collective responsibility within multi-member constitutional commissions while preserving administrative agility during complex revision exercises like the SIR.

news.mains_notes:
### Institutional Governance & Decision-Making in ECI
- **Constitutional Basis:** Article 324 grants superintendence, direction, and control over electoral roll preparation to the ECI.
- **Statutory Framework:** Section 18 of the 2023 Act establishes that decisions should be unanimous or taken by majority consensus.
- **Statutory vs Administrative Changes:** Under Section 28 of RPA 1950, statutory rules and forms require Central Government notification and parliamentary tabling. Administrative annexures (e.g., Annexure IV during SIR) serve as temporary verification tools without altering statutory instruments like Form 6.
mains_questions: Examine the constitutional and statutory mechanism governing decision-making within the Election Commission of India in light of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023.
Distinguish between statutory rule-making under the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and administrative directions issued under Article 324 of the Constitution.
news.takeaway: The ECI confirmed to the Supreme Court that all SIR decisions were made unanimously under Section 18 of the 2023 Act, and clarified that additional voter declarations were separate administrative documents rather than amendments to statutory Form 6.

Section 28 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 governs rule-making powers.
Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023 mandates unanimous or majority decisions in ECI.
The affidavit in SC was submitted through Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu.

hindi_translation.story_lead: भारत निर्वाचन आयोग (ECI) ने सर्वोच्च न्यायालय में एक संयुक्त जवाबी हलफनामा दायर कर कहा कि विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR) से जुड़े सभी तीन आदेश इसके तीनों सदस्यों द्वारा सर्वसम्मति से लिए गए थे। चुनाव निकाय ने उन आरोपों को खारिज कर दिया कि मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार ने एकतरफा कार्रवाई की थी या मतदाता पंजीकरण नियमों का उल्लंघन किया गया था।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### सर्वोच्च न्यायालय में ईसीआई का हलफनामा: मुख्य बिंदु और वैधानिक तर्क

उप चुनाव आयुक्त भानु प्रकाश येतुरु के माध्यम से दायर एक संयुक्त जवाबी हलफनामे में, भारत निर्वाचन आयोग—मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार और चुनाव आयुक्त सुखबीर सिंह संधू और विवेक जोशी—ने मतदाता सूचियों के विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR) के दौरान एकतरफा निर्णय लेने के आरोपों को पूरी तरह खारिज कर दिया। यह प्रतिक्रिया लोकसभा में विपक्ष के नेता राहुल गांधी के नेतृत्व वाले विपक्षी नेताओं द्वारा दायर याचिकाओं के जवाब में आई है, जिसमें ईसीआई के कामकाज की न्यायिक जांच की मांग की गई थी।

### प्रमुख तथ्य और वैधानिक बिंदु:
- **निर्णयों में सर्वसम्मति:** ईसीआई ने पुष्टि की कि 24 जून 2025, 27 अक्टूबर 2025 और 14 मई 2026 के तीनों एसआईआर आदेश संविधान के अनुच्छेद 324 और मुख्य निर्वाचन आयुक्त और अन्य निर्वाचन आयुक्त अधिनियम, 2023 की धारा 18 के तहत सर्वसम्मत निर्णयों के अनुसार जारी किए गए थे।
- **फॉर्म 6 की स्थिति:** आयोग ने स्पष्ट किया कि मतदाता पंजीकरण नियम, 1960 के तहत नए मतदाताओं के नामांकन के लिए उपयोग किए जाने वाले वैधानिक फॉर्म 6 में कोई संशोधन नहीं किया गया। एसआईआर के दौरान आवश्यक अतिरिक्त घोषणापत्र (शुरुआत में अनुलग्नक D और बाद में अनुलग्नक IV) एक अलग प्रशासनिक दस्तावेज था, न कि वैधानिक फॉर्म का संशोधन।
- **अतिरिक्त घोषणा का उद्देश्य:** यह घोषणापत्र आवेदकों को पिछली मतदाता सूचियों (या माता-पिता/दादा-दादी के विवरण) से जुड़ने की सुविधा देता था ताकि दावे और आपत्तियों के चरण के दौरान सहायक दस्तावेज प्रस्तुत करने की आवश्यकता न पड़े।
- **वैधानिक संशोधन प्रक्रिया:** लोक प्रतिनिधित्व अधिनियम, 1950 की धारा 28 के तहत वैधानिक नियमों या फॉर्मों में किसी भी संशोधन को ईसीआई के परामर्श से केंद्र सरकार द्वारा अधिसूचित और संसद के समक्ष प्रस्तुत किया जाना आवश्यक है। ईसीआई ने तर्क दिया कि फॉर्म 6 स्वयं अपरिवर्तित रहा, इसलिए इस प्रक्रिया की आवश्यकता नहीं थी।
- **आंतरिक विचार-विमर्श बनाम अंतिम निर्णय:** ईसीआई ने कहा कि आयुक्तों द्वारा विचार-विमर्श के दौरान उठाए गए विचार या आपत्तियां अपने आप में अधिनियम की धारा 18 के तहत निर्णय नहीं बनाती हैं। निर्णय औपचारिक बैठकों या फाइलों पर दर्ज होकर अंतिम रूप लेते हैं।
hindi_translation.background_context: यह मामला देशव्यापी एसआईआर अभ्यास की वैधता और मीडिया रिपोर्टों के आधार पर दायर याचिकाओं से जुड़ा है, जिनमें दावा किया गया था कि दो चुनाव आयुक्तों ने 14 अवसरों पर असहमति जताई थी।
bullet_points: ईसीआई ने मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार और आयुक्तों सुखबीर सिंह संधू व विवेक जोशी की ओर से संयुक्त हलफनामा दायर किया।
हलफनामे में कहा गया है कि तीनों एसआईआर आदेश सर्वसम्मति से पारित किए गए थे।
ईसीआई ने मतदाता पंजीकरण नियम, 1960 के तहत फॉर्म 6 में किसी भी संशोधन से इनकार किया।
अतिरिक्त घोषणा (अनुलग्नक IV) एसआईआर के लिए केवल एक अस्थायी प्रशासनिक दस्तावेज था।
2023 अधिनियम की धारा 18 के तहत निर्णय सर्वसम्मति या बहुमत से लिए जाने का प्रावधान है।
लोक प्रतिनिधित्व अधिनियम, 1950 की धारा 28 के तहत नियम बनाने की शक्ति केंद्र सरकार के पास है।
विपक्षी नेताओं ने एसआईआर पर रोक और न्यायिक जांच की मांग की थी।
ईसीआई ने स्पष्ट किया कि 29 जुलाई 2026 का पत्राचार अधिकारी की प्रतिनियुक्ति से संबंधित था, नीतिगत निर्णयों से नहीं।

संबंधित अधिनियम: मुख्य निर्वाचन आयुक्त और अन्य निर्वाचन आयुक्त अधिनियम, 2023 (धारा 18)।

quiz.question: Which section of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 empowers the Central Government to frame rules, such as the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, in consultation with the Election Commission?
quiz.correct_answer: Section 28
quiz.explanation: Section 28 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 empowers the Central Government, after consulting the Election Commission, to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, under which the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 were framed.
